biography: Garrett "The Hammer" Adams didn't grow up karting like most. He was wrenching on his dad's beat-up Ford pickup in rural Oklahoma, learning to coax every last ounce of performance from a machine. His racing career started late, at 23, in local dirt track events. His raw talent was immediately apparent. A defining moment came when he won the Oklahoma State Dirt Track Championship in his second season, beating veterans who had been racing for decades. That victory earned him a scholarship to a regional racing school, paving the way for his eventual move to sports car racing. Now, at 37, driving for Lamborghini, Adams is seen as a talented but inconsistent driver. His aggressive style sometimes yields brilliant results, but also costly mistakes, leading many to believe he's past his prime and struggling to adapt to the modern racing landscape. He's fighting hard to prove them wrong, one late-braking maneuver at a time.
drivingStyle: Adams is a late-braking, aggressive driver who isn't afraid to push the limits of the car – and sometimes beyond. He thrives in wet conditions, where his car control skills shine. He's known for his daring overtakes, often diving down the inside into corners where others wouldn't dare. Tire management isn't his strongest suit; he tends to overdrive the car early in a stint, sacrificing long-run pace for immediate gains. Under pressure, Adams can either elevate his game or crack, depending on the day. It's a volatile mix that makes him an exciting, if unpredictable, competitor.

rivalries.reason: Bellini, a smooth and calculated Italian driver, represents everything Adams isn't. Their contrasting styles often lead to on-track clashes, and a simmering resentment exists between them.
